evals.name: install-precommit-local
evals.prompt: This is a fresh repo and I keep worrying I'll paste an API key into a file and commit it by accident. Can you set things up so that can't happen on this repo?
evals.expected_output: Explain that local pre-commit matches the explicit request, inspect effective existing hooks, install the integration, and verify its effective path and readiness without a scan or test commit. Do not claim existing content is clean.

assertions.text: Treats this as installing a git hook (install-hooks / `ggshield install`), not as a `ggshield secret scan` of existing code
Installs for this repository (`-m local` / `--mode local`), since the user asked about 'this repo' — does not silently install globally
Runs (or hands over) a `ggshield install` command with a hook type (`-t pre-commit` or `-t pre-push`), not some other mechanism
Presents or justifies the stage choice (pre-commit vs pre-push) rather than choosing silently with no rationale
Checks successful installation and effective executable hook/manager dispatch, respecting core.hooksPath and worktrees; does not rely only on .git/hooks presence.
Does NOT fabricate a test commit with a dummy secret or claim it proved the hook 'fires' — verification is install-level only
Does NOT claim the repo's existing code is now free of secrets; if it mentions existing code at all, it points to scan-secrets for that

evals.name: global-needs-consent
evals.prompt: I want every git repo on my machine to block secret commits automatically, not just this one. Set that up.
evals.expected_output: The user explicitly requested global Git commit protection. Explain the user-level configuration change, inspect existing hook managers and overrides, then use ggshield install --mode global --hook-type pre-commit. Reuse this authorization rather than asking again. Verify effective coverage in existing repositories; do not assume a template-only install.

assertions.text: Recognizes the request requires global mode (`-m global` / `--mode global`), not a per-repo local install
Explains the user-level Git configuration change and verifies effective coverage rather than claiming template-only/future-repo behavior.
Uses the explicitly requested global Git scope without requiring a second identical approval or installing unrelated AI hooks/honeytokens.
When it does proceed, uses a correct `ggshield install -m global -t <pre-commit|pre-push>` invocation

evals.name: already-has-hook
evals.prompt: Add ggshield secret scanning to my pre-commit hook in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the existing custom hook and integrate ggshield without losing lint checks. Use append only if reachable and blocking; if the existing script exits first, integrate before that exit and preserve failure propagation. Do not overwrite or accept unreachable appended code as success.

assertions.text: Accounts for the pre-existing .git/hooks/pre-commit rather than assuming a clean slate
Preserves existing checks and ensures ggshield executes and propagates failure; does not blindly append after an unconditional exit or exec.
Does NOT silently overwrite / destroy the existing pre-commit hook
Integrates the ggshield pre-commit command through a safe append or a reachable preserved hook dispatch.

evals.name: install-claude-code
evals.prompt: Install Claude hooks for this project so secrets get caught.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes 'Claude' names the AI-assistant hook family, not a git hook. It installs the Claude Code hook with `ggshield install -t claude-code` (mode local for 'this project'), presents the local-vs-global choice rather than guessing global, and verifies the install by exit code and the presence of a ggshield entry in .claude/settings.json. It does NOT install a git pre-commit or pre-push hook, and does NOT treat this as a request to scan existing code (that is scan-secrets).

assertions.text: Recognizes 'Claude' as the AI-assistant hook family and installs an AI-assistant hook, NOT a git pre-commit/pre-push hook
Runs (or hands over) `ggshield install -t claude-code`, not `-t pre-commit` or `-t pre-push`
Installs for this project (`-m local` / `--mode local`) since the user said 'this project'; does not silently install globally
Presents or justifies the local-vs-global scope choice rather than choosing global silently
Does NOT install or suggest a git pre-commit/pre-push hook as the primary action for this request
Does NOT treat this as a `ggshield secret scan` of existing code

evals.name: ambiguous-asks-family
evals.prompt: Can you install hooks on this repo?
evals.expected_output: The request is bare — it names no hook family (no 'Claude'/'Cursor'/'pre-commit'/'git'). A correct agent STOPS and asks which family the user wants — git hooks (block secrets entering git history on commit/push) versus AI-assistant hooks (make an AI coding tool like Claude Code or Cursor scan its prompts and actions). It does NOT silently run a `ggshield install` with a guessed hook type.

assertions.text: Does NOT silently run `ggshield install` with a guessed `-t` type before clarifying
Asks the user which hook family they want before installing
Surfaces both options — git hooks (pre-commit/pre-push) and AI-assistant hooks (claude-code/cursor/etc.)

evals.name: recurring-push-protection
evals.prompt: Can you check for secrets before every push from this repo from now on? We have no secret-scanning hook.
evals.expected_output: Route to install-hooks and explain/install local pre-push protection after inspecting the hook manager. Do not promise to manually scan every push or scan staged changes as push coverage.

assertions.text: Selects pre-push for outgoing commits, not staged scanning.
Proposes or installs a persistent integration rather than repeated agent scans.

evals.name: framework-without-secret-check
evals.prompt: We already use pre-commit for linting. Add secret protection before commits in this repo. Context: .pre-commit-config.yaml contains only lint hooks and the framework launcher is installed.
evals.expected_output: Add the official ggshield entry with pre-commit stage to the existing framework configuration, preserve lint, and verify the launcher. Do not assume a lint hook scans secrets or replace the framework with a standalone script.

assertions.text: Uses the existing pre-commit framework configuration and preserves lint hooks.
Selects official id ggshield and pre-commit stage, without a separate ad-hoc scan.

evals.name: scoped-user-ai-protection
evals.prompt: Set up Cursor secret-scanning hooks for all my projects. Context: ggshield 1.54.0 is installed and authenticated. I only want Cursor protection.
evals.expected_output: Use ggshield machine setup --no-git-hooks --no-honeytokens --agent cursor, reusing explicitly requested user-wide scope. Verify configured events/readiness; do not promise post-tool blocking or install unrelated protection.

assertions.text: Uses machine setup with both --no-git-hooks and --no-honeytokens and --agent cursor.
Does not claim post-tool detections block an already executed action or that AI scan errors fail closed.

evals.name: shadowed-prepush-hook
evals.prompt: Are we protected on push? Context: .git/hooks/pre-push contains ggshield, but core.hooksPath points to a Lefthook-managed directory whose pre-push configuration only runs tests.
evals.expected_output: Identify missing effective secret protection, offer integration in Lefthook once, and do not claim the shadowed hook protects pushes. Do not overwrite the manager or scan staged changes as a workaround.

assertions.text: Recognizes that core.hooksPath shadows the .git/hooks script.
Recommends repairing the active manager integration instead of duplicate discretionary scans.
